**Last checked:** 2026-11-12, against `phase1/planar` at `0da97ba` in
`Symplectomorphism/c-gnn`. The full records are in the discussion
compendium (`reports/supporting_docs/discussion-compendium/`); commits are on that branch.

## Open

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## The realizer plans held poses, not stick–slip plans (open, Nov 12)
Λ<sub>qs</sub> plans positions only and models forces as the gate's hold test
at each knot (both edges of every cone): a sequence of static holds, Theorem
B's level. With its two path fixes (`disk_path_fix`, `roll_press_fix`, on by
default) the chain search solves the indirect lift at μ = 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5;
without them the disk slid down the face in break(m<sub>x</sub>) and the
search failed at 0.3. Decided: the gate stays at the hold level. A stick–slip
variant of the realizer is built (`stick_slip`, off): it realizes 9–12 fewer
of 227 replayed calls per μ and its chain search fails at 0.3, so it stays
off.
[The local solver](local-solver.qmd#qs-slip).
:::

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## The search does not find the indirect lift by itself (open; the target)
The indirect lift, held at every instant, is the paper's running chain; its
last four edits and closing transport are certified over μ ∈ [0.3, 0.5].
Given only its formation sequence, the planner realizes it from rest at
μ = 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 (Λ<sub>qs</sub> with its path fixes). From the scene
alone it does not find it yet: the bottleneck is exploration and a value
that orders the search (learning and exploration below). The gate's
earlier refusal of the disk's transfer round the box's corner was a bug in the
relaxed gate, fixed by H1 (`relax_untouched`).
[Results](../results/index.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## The open work, in order (the compendium's board, Nov 11–12)
1. **Parametric certificate of the support LP.** Certify a hold along a whole
   path, not at sampled poses: the transport gate (it replaces the grid and the
   temporary ±20 cm push range the end-to-end runs needed; at the stock ±5 cm
   range the lift to a set place solved 0 of 10), the lazy target query (an
   exclusion certificate) and the realizer (held between plan knots). Queued
   with it: a polynomial (sum-of-squares) certificate for large regions and an
   online tube certificate of the next segment in Λ<sub>qs</sub>'s receding
   horizon.
2. **H2, certified execution** (the measured bottleneck): plan knots held
   throughout, admissible end knots, a tracking bound, the free-approach
   window; the pushes that stop 3–5 mm short (`slide_lag` stays until then).
3. **H3, a judge that measures "held"**: the hold margin along the trajectory
   instead of the 6 mm kinetic-energy threshold for dynamic events.
4. **A3, the uncertainty model**: ε by a 95/95 bound, the μ band's
   robustness, ε<sub>pen</sub>.
5. **Gate decisions (Aykut)**: the target threshold (R4); when an edit must
   close locally; the lazy query's exclusion certificate; a gate whose
   necessity needs no Lipschitz or covering hypothesis (refuse only where the
   interval certificate proves "not held").
6. **A value that only orders** (H4): lexicographic value, edge lengths from
   measured calls, the η<sub>max</sub> sweep; a derived replacement for the
   progress threshold δ = 10 mm, which rests on the declared merge radius.
7. **Learning and exploration**, after held solves exist: π mixing, Go-Explore
   restarts, V₁ with a certified Lipschitz bound, the attention ranker,
   retrained on held solves.
8. **Releases R1–R3**: a proposal; releases are off until then.
9. **Discovery and scenes**: a taller step (H = a/2), the scene families, then
   a second disk.
10. **The headline rerun** at the band's ends (μ = 0.3 and 0.5), with every
    rule of the paper's search on (the reported runs had the workspace and
    dynamic-event rules off; an audit of their solves found no end either rule
    rejects).
11. **The RL skills**: retraining over μ ~ U[0.3, 0.5] is in progress (tests
    pinned to 0.99 until it lands); whether the break skill stays in the method
    or becomes an ablation is Aykut's call, as is the recognizer rethink.
12. **Housekeeping**: JAX loops (the gate takes 20–35 s per call on GPU).
:::

[]{#eps-pen}

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Ties under deep overlap (ε<sub>pen</sub> = 5 mm is provisional)
ε<sub>pen</sub> is ten times ε<sub>on</sub>, so both corners of a tilted box
edge can count as touching. 475 of 4,000 demo poses jittered by about 3 mm
are ambiguous (474 with a contact deeper than ε<sub>on</sub>; in 136,
s<sub>v</sub> loses to t, which contains it). A tied pose is never a search
node or a solver success, so no wrong label is used; the stress test's
budget is 500, set for those 475 ties at ε<sub>pen</sub> = 10 mm and loose at
today's 257. Since step 3b ε<sub>pen</sub> = 5 mm (257 ties); 2–3 mm
(44–98 ties) needs stiffer contacts, which keep penetration under 0.22 mm
but need the controller retuned first. [Contact states](contact-states.qmd#the-recognizer).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## The 3D hold LP needs reinversion (frozen with 3D)
Float32 rounding builds up in linrax's dense tableau over the long pivot
sequences of 3D cones: about 1% of supported 3D cases end "uncertain"
(rejected, never certified wrongly), and `test_3d_cones_finish_and_never_mislead`
fails on the GPU. The cure is rebuilding the tableau from the final basis. The
project is planar; 3D is frozen. [Background](support-tutorial.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## Resolved

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Decided Nov 11–12: friction band, certified margin, the realizer's defaults
- **Disk friction is a declared band**, μ<sub>disk</sub> ∈ [0.3, 0.5], one
  model everywhere (the simulator's 0.99 was a model-file number, not a
  measurement; the gate and tracker had used 0.35). The simulator runs at 0.3
  (0.5 with `CMG_DISK_FRICTION`); the gate and the tracker use 0.3.
- **The gate's margin is a certified bound.** A float32 exit program that
  failed its check had counted as exit 0 and made the refusal "certified";
  now "held" needs a witness and "not held" a Farkas certificate, else
  uncertain. On 10<sup>6</sup> pivot poses, 5 false refusals became 0.
- **The gate stays at the hold level**; stick or slip belongs to the
  realizer's plan.
- **The support clause matches the theory**: σ̄ must hold before the
  transition, σ̲ from it on.
- **Transfers close as makes do** (`transfer_close_local` on): χ<sub>tr</sub>
  is where the added contact touches.
- **Λ<sub>qs</sub>'s feed-forward is the minimum-norm holding force.** The Nov 11
  "moving force" (`ff_push`) was retracted: every force the hold LP admits is an
  equilibrium force, so none moves the box; the box moves because the
  reference moves.
- **Λ<sub>qs</sub>'s options `roll_pivot`, `ff0_hold`, `settle_ext` and
  `qs_plan_check` are the default**; `ff_push`, `ff_interior`, `fn_preload`,
  `cone_proj` and `sequence_count` were removed (kept on branch
  `night/roll-2026-11-11`).
- **H1 merged** (the corner refusal of the relaxed gate fixed, admissible poses,
  the held component and lazy targets); its flags 1–4 off by default, the
  transfer closing rule on. **Certified placement** is in the code behind
  `chi_t_rule="certified"` (off); the **stick–slip executor** is in scripts.
- **The RL skills are retrained over the band** (decided; in progress).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Lowering the box off the platform (solved by the redesign with releases on)
With the redesign (a push toward the edge, then a release) the teacher lowered
40 of 40 instances; paired with CMGMP at 1,800 s, 25 against 24 of 25 (simulator
disk friction 0.99, gate 0.35). Releases are now off pending a principled
release (R1–R3), so in the current configuration lowering waits for it. Before
the redesign no lowering was solved (0/40): the only edit off the platform was
a balance Λ<sub>qs</sub> could not hold. [Search](search.qmd#redesign).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Decided Nov 9: the redesign (results on [the results page](../results/archive.qmd#nov10))
The settle clause is off for formation edits (reported separately) and
required for releases and the final goal state. The tie rule and the roll skill
are shelved (off, kept as a variant of Λ). Lowering: a push toward the edge,
then a release (releases are now off, above). Retries from other nodes of a
key are for the teacher only; the planner and every reported result use none.
The search gets outcome children, box moves within a contact state and releases
as actions, and PHS\* ordered by a value. The 125 mm gap screen is dropped.
The creep of a box at rest in MJX came from pyramidal friction cones and is
gone with elliptic cones. [Search](search.qmd#redesign).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The search's defects at `phase1/dev` (fixed Nov 8, Decision 18)
Angelo's `Search` accepted when the requested contacts were in band, ignoring
the solver's success flag; a node stored the requested formation, not the one
reached; a break was accepted without checking that the contact left; there
was no goal test, goal input or budget. Now a call counts only if Λ succeeds
and the recognizer returns exactly the requested formation, the child stores
the recognized formation, and the search has goals and a call budget.
Walkthrough [8](../code-walkthrough/08-search.qmd) (archived) shows the old
behaviour.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The hold tests are float32 (resolved: γ<sub>min</sub> and the certified margin)
The gate agreed with a float64 reference on 1,000 of 1,000 random cases and on
every near-boundary case 0.33 mm or more from the boundary; its only misses
were acceptances with margin 0 (at most 2·10<sup>−7</sup>) at the boundary
pose itself. The acceptance threshold γ<sub>min</sub> = 10<sup>−5</sup> removes
them, and since Nov 11 the margin is a certified lower bound.
[The hold gate](hold-gate.qmd#accuracy).
:::

The gate now asks whether *some* disk position in the disk's region holds the

states differing only in where the disk sits are one node. Measured against

## The hard break(g<sub>v</sub>): a learned skill (Nov 8–9, `9e7211f`); measured at disk friction 0.99
The quasi-static realizers failed it because the box's corners slide. SAC
trained from scratch in the MJX simulator solves 18/18 hard and 150/150

Whether the skill stays in the method or becomes an ablation is open.
[The local solver](local-solver.qmd#learned-skill).

The teacher's failed transfers and disk makes were real realizer failures, now

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Cluster jobs died with "LLVM: Cannot allocate memory" (Nov 8, `1e6fce8`)
Juno and Ganymede2 cap a process at 65,530 memory mappings (this workstation
allows 1,048,576). The gate ran outside `jit`, so XLA compiled one module per
operation and shape: seven gate calls in one test added 78,000 mappings. With
the gate jitted inside `Cand`, they add 11,000; the full test suite on Juno
went from about 10 to 3.6 minutes, with no failures. A guard
(`cmg.mapguard`) clears JAX's caches if a long process nears the limit.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The graph W is a neighbor graph; merging by evaluation (Nov 8, Decision 19)
Single changes now need the two formations to be realized within 25 mm of each
other (as compound edges already did), formations must be recognizable, and
vertex–vertex contacts appear only alone. W has 328 formations, 2,398 single
and 92 compound edges; the pivot stays compound. Certified constants gave a
merge radius under 1 mm, so duplicates are merged only when the gate gives
equal verdicts (within a 10 mm test radius). [Node identity](node-identity.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Node identity: from a rounded pose to formation + disk region + box pose (Nov 8, Decisions 17 and 18)
The search keyed nodes by their formation and a pose rounded to 1 mm /
0.01 rad cells, a placeholder from the first search stub that Decision 9
(adopting Xiao and Ji) never revisited. The paper noticed the gap and
recorded it instead of raising it; an audit then found nine more unrecorded
divergences from Xiao and Ji, decided in Decision 18. Xiao and Ji's contact
state (formation + connected region) assumes a driven object; our box moves
only when the disk pushes it, so the key collapses only the disk's region
and keeps the box's pose, merged within a margin-certified radius. Nothing
is snapped. Explained with worked examples on [Node identity](node-identity.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Step 3d choices decided; the sweep is now adaptive (Nov 8, Decision 16, `84b7ab2`)
The friction cap stayed unset (superseded the next day by the gate's disk

candidates against a dense reference: at the simulator's friction every

[The sweep's resolution](local-solver.qmd#sweep-resolution).

[]{#sweep-basis}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The gate's sweep probed different poses on the CPU and the GPU (Nov 8, `f54dc73`)
The transition sweep's grid followed the SVD's null vectors, which are any
rotation of a basis when two or more directions are free; the CPU and the
GPU returned different rotations. Harmless at μ = 0.99, decisive at 0.35.
Now a canonical basis of the subspace (pivoted Gram–Schmidt on its
projector); the backends agree, and a test rotates the basis and checks
nothing changes.
:::

[]{#gap-sign}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The GPU's −96 mm gap was a float32 sliver in the penetration attribution (Nov 8)
At the landed pose with the box's top face almost parallel to the riser,
the box's lower corner sits 2·10⁻⁸ m inside the platform (float32 noise).
That penetration belongs to the platform, the nearer segment, but on the
GPU a one-ulp piece of the face, λ ∈ [0.99999994, 1], stayed attributed to
the riser: it has no representable midpoint, so the strict "another
segment is closer" test was evaluated at its end and failed, and the
sliver carried the riser's h = −96 mm as its depth. Fix: attributed pieces
narrower than 10⁻⁶ (in λ) are dropped; CPU and GPU now agree (+96.24 mm),
and the pose is a test (`test_gap_sign_near_parallel_resting_box`).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Exact validity and the local compound rule (Nov 8, Decisions 11, 12, 14; merge `9ea09bb`)
Validity now comes from the geometry: a certified table of the 357
formations some admissible pose realizes (the stand-in admitted 37,203),
from 552 excluded pairs and 4 triples. Compound edges follow the local rule
by default (Decision 14): no intermediate is realized within ρ = 25 mm of
the transition pose. On the step scene that gives 96 compound instances
(the global rule 136; the dropped 40 join formations realized 85–184 mm
apart, which no single motion connects); the pivot stays compound. The
global rule stays selectable. [Edits](edits.qmd).
:::

[]{#safe-pruning}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Duplicate keys: safe pruning and canonical states, so the call bound holds (Nov 8, Decision 13)
The theory note proves that the search makes at most min ν/π calls of Λ
(Orseau and Lelis's policy-guided search bound). With duplicate node keys
the bound needs two things: nodes of one key behave alike (one canonical
state per key, the first one made) and the *safe* rule: drop a new child
only if a node already made with its key has π at least as large;
otherwise make it as a new node. First-come pruning breaks the bound
(17,664 calls against 10,020 in the theory note's example); so does
re-parenting the existing node to the higher-π arrival (26 against 22.2
in a small example). Implemented in `cmg/search` (`SearchState`,
`PolicyRanker`) with both examples as tests. *The canonical states were
later withdrawn: with the node key of Decision 17 every node keeps its real
state; the safe rule stays.*
:::

[]{#replan-defect}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Re-planning restarted the change at every re-plan (Nov 8, `7e2234f`)
The first re-planning version gave every new plan the time the open-loop
plan had left, re-swept χ<sub>tr</sub>, and re-planned phase I while the box
was still recognized as σ, which it is until the change completes. The
change was pushed to the last steps and made fast: make(s) and
transfer(s<sub>v</sub> → t) failed by overshoot, and re-planning was worse
than open loop. Fixed: each phase keeps its scheduled end, χ<sub>tr</sub> is
kept, and once the plan has passed χ<sub>tr</sub> the previous plan continues
until σ′ is recognized. [The local solver](local-solver.qmd#step-3c).
:::

[]{#step3-decided}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Step-3 choices decided: the mode-scheduled realizer, cost E, ε<sub>pen</sub> = 5 mm, thresholds (Nov 7, `767ab7a`, `6dec516`)
Aykut chose a mode-scheduled quasi-static realizer with tracking in MuJoCo
(Λ<sub>qs</sub>) over MPPI, which stays as the baseline with cost E (the
paper's terms over ε<sub>on</sub>); ε<sub>pen</sub> = 5 mm; χ<sub>tr</sub> the
nearest swept pose with margin ≥ γ<sub>tr</sub> = 0.1; acceptance at margin ≥
γ<sub>min</sub> = 10⁻⁵; the sweep's defaults. Λ<sub>qs</sub> realizes every
chain edit from its canonical start, including the pivot and
break(g<sub>v</sub>) at 45°, which no MPPI cost realized (checkpoint 2: 23 of
25, against 13 of 25 for MPPI-E). [The local solver](local-solver.qmd#lambda-qs).
:::

[]{#decision-9}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Xiao and Ji's construction adopted (Nov 7, `9261ece`)
Our construction had drifted from Xiao and Ji's contact formations in ways
that were conveniences, not needs. A literature search (13 papers read in
full) found nothing simpler that still meets our needs: stances,
body-pair strata and scene graphs cannot see a box tip from its edge onto
its corner; configuration-space cells and triangulated subcontacts split one
motion into several edges. We now follow Xiao and Ji exactly and add only
tolerances, several bodies with a manipulator, and a no-contact state per
pair.

| | Before (`84827c0`) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Environment | three convex bodies; the step corner owned by the riser | one polygon E; convex vertices from the geometry |
| Contacts per pair | at most one per body pair | at most one per pair of convex elements, none alongside one it contains |
| Transfers | same or adjacent features: 92 pairs, only 48 Xiao–Ji neighbors | one-sided containment: 56 pairs |
| Compound edges | two transfers in different body pairs | all relaxing or all constraining, every proper subset invalid (same 128 on the step) |
| Valid formations | 11,959 of 12,393 | 37,203 of 59,049 |

The landed box became {t} (next entry). [Contact states](contact-states.qmd), [edits](edits.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The landed box is {t}, not {s<sub>v</sub>, t} (Nov 7, accepted by Aykut)
Once +x<sub>B</sub> lies on the platform, v<sub>S</sub> bounds the touching
platform edge, so s<sub>v</sub> is not principal. Landing is
transfer(s<sub>v</sub> → t), sliding off the corner is transport, and the
chain is one edit shorter. Support is unchanged. [Edits](edits.qmd#the-step-chain).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Transfers, the disk around a corner, corner ownership (Nov 7, `9261ece`)
- 44 of the 92 old transfers were not Xiao–Ji neighbors: 20 went round a
  corner in one step, 24 changed both features at once. Transfers are now
  one-sided containment only (56).
- The disk goes round a box corner in two transfers, through its contact
  with the vertex.
- No ownership rule is needed: the environment is one object whose convex
  vertices come from its geometry (this replaces the Nov 5 rule that the
  riser owns the step corner).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Compound edges: the two-transfer rule, then the general rule (Nov 7, `5b25385`, `9261ece`)
The pivot needs g → g<sub>v</sub> and s → s<sub>v</sub> together, since both
one-at-a-time intermediates are excluded. Settled first as a closed form
(two transfers in different body pairs with crossed exclusions), it was
replaced the same day by Xiao and Ji's neighbor relation with the minimality
rule, which gives the same edges on the step and needs no special case.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The gate tests the less-constrained end; a transfer keeps the old normal (Nov 7, `a3789d7`, `9261ece`)
H first tested the contacts that persist through an edit, with the old
contact's normal for a transfer (on the demo the two normals differ by at
most 1.77° where it matters; using the new one changes none of 1,155
decisions). Under Xiao and Ji's containment both follow from one rule: test
the edit's less-constrained end, as multi-contact planners do (Hauser et
al. 2005, 2008; Escande et al. 2013); the normal comes from the feature that
stays.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The margin and the gate's solver (Nov 7, `228950f`)
The margin is set inclusion of a disturbance polytope, by default the ℓ₁
ball (0.2 = μ on the flat box). The disk's force is bounded by its motors
(±1 N, read from the MuJoCo model), which also made margins with the disk
finite; before, its unbounded push made the support cone fill all of 3D.
The LP backbone is the gate; the exact cone test is its cross-check.
[The hold gate](hold-gate.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The gate at χ₀ refused realizable edits (Nov 7, `41b5721`, `26c96d0`)
break(g<sub>v</sub>) was refused at 30° although tilting further and then
lifting is possible. H now searches near χ₀ over the more-constrained end's
contacts for a transition pose where the less-constrained end holds, and
passes it to the solver. Pose distances use the paper's weight a/2 on
angles. [The hold gate](hold-gate.qmd#sweep).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## One success test for every realizer (Nov 7, `41b5721`)
MPPI graded itself with its own gap-band test. Every realizer now uses the
paper's success test, extended to transfers and compound edges.
[The local solver](local-solver.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The paper rewritten on the current construction (Nov 7, `e2f705c` to `63de648`)
The old draft (archived, tag `paper-v1-2026-11-07`) described corner
ownership, one contact per body pair, the old chain and stale numbers for
h = a/4. The paper was rewritten from scratch and revised after four
independent reviews; the proofs that the gate never refuses a realizable
edit and that the recognizer is correct are in its appendices.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The hold LPs in float32 with linrax (Nov 6, `e29d96f`, `b354251`)
- linrax had no iteration cap and could cycle on degenerate 3D LPs, hanging
  a whole `vmap` batch: its pivot loop is replaced (300 pivots per phase,
  Bland's leaving rule, artificial rows marked correctly).
- It returned infeasible points as optimal in float32: fixed by
  Householder-spread rows, primal and dual from the final basis, pivot
  tolerance 10<sup>−4</sup>, exit cap 10, and every answer checked.
- linrax has no license file; accepted (Aykut, Nov 6), pinned to 0.3.0.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Step 2's foundations (Nov 5, `d810e32`, `1986c73`)
- `Cand` had no validity check (a second contact per pair, excluded
  formations, transport always legal): edits now pass validity, transfer and
  compound rules; transport only when supported.
- No transfer generator: g → g<sub>v</sub> needed a break and a make through
  a formation where the box does not touch the floor.
- MPAX's "not supported" was uncertified (192–194 of 416 supported
  near-boundary cases rejected): replaced by the exact cone test with
  witness and certificate, later by the LP gate.
- The cone test's margin was positive on a single-ray cone and failed below
  three generators: fixed, and the margin proved to be the signed distance.
- JAX's reduced-precision (TF32) GPU products broke the supporting-plane
  checks: dot products are formed elementwise.
- Tied poses are treated as ambiguous: never a node or a solver success.
:::

[]{#theta-e}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The edge-contact tilt θ<sub>e</sub> (Nov 5, `5f5a2e8`)
A length rule ("flat if 7.8 mm lie within 1 mm") called a box tipped 7.35°
flat, and as the box tipped over the step corner it switched the floor
contact at 7.35° but the riser contact at 8.44°, labeling the impossible
{g<sub>v</sub>, s} in between. An angle shared by both contacts fixes this.
Two principled options were compared: the engines' point rule (both ends of
the overlap within 1 mm), which switches floor and riser at 0.46° and 1.83°
and realizes {g<sub>v</sub>, s} on 13 demo frames; and one derived angle,
θ<sub>e</sub> = arcsin(ε<sub>on</sub>/h) ≈ 1.83°, which switches both together
and is exactly the point rule on the riser. The derived angle was adopted
(a 2° value tuned to the demo, `62782b8`, was withdrawn). Hysteresis for
trajectory labels was deferred to the execution monitor.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Step 1's foundations (Nov 4–5, `ca4123b`, `b2665cb`, `583810b`)
- One physical contact lit 3 to 6 template bits (closed features share
  boundaries): replaced by the principal-contact recognizer.
- The hold test used one tie-broken point per contact, blended by
  smoothing, and ±y faces on a planar body: replaced by the contact sets'
  endpoints in a planar catalog.
- Exclusions were integer indices, then dropped; there were no vertex
  features for g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>: named templates and vertices in
  `step2d.yaml`.
- Overlaps were charged to the wrong surface (−31 mm into the platform):
  each overlap is charged to the nearest environment segment or endpoint
  (approved Nov 5).
- A Python loop over templates: one `vmap` per kernel (the 3D catalog still
  loops).
- NaN gradients in the planar kernels: safe norms and roots.
- The tie-break was kept as the recognizer's fallback, with every use
  counted.
- `pyproject.toml` was invalid TOML: fixed upstream.
:::
